title: Fluorescence-based protocol for revealing cellular arrangement in biofilms
protocol: Grow biofilms using 96-well microtitre plate static assays.
Fill wells of microtitre plates with 200 μL of fresh LB containing a 1:10 dilution of overnight cultures, mixed in a 1:10 ratio of green and red fluorescent cells.
Carefully break 18 × 18 mm cover glass into pieces big enough to fit inside the wells of a microtitre plate.
Break cover glass into pieces by taking 3-4 cover glass squares and using a glass slide as support.
Sterilize cover glass pieces by autoclaving.
Insert sterilized cover glass pieces perpendicularly inside the wells for biofilm growth.
Incubate plates overnight (16–24 h) or for desired duration for biofilm formation without shaking at 37°C.
Use tweezers to carefully remove the cover glass piece from a well for biofilm imaging.
Lay the cover glass piece flat on a fresh glass slide.
Label the glass slide with any necessary cell names or conditions being tested.
Wait for at least one minute before placing a fresh cover glass over the biofilm-covered glass piece.
Apply the 22 × 50 mm cover glass at approximately a 45° angle, starting from the air to the liquid portion of the covered glass piece.
Set up glass slide, prepared in steps 6–9, on the microscope for imaging.
Focus on the biofilms formed on the cover glass pieces.
Capture a wide-field view of the biofilms using red and green fluorescence channels.
Image biofilms at high magnification to resolve their structures at the cellular level.
Use LASX software to overlay images captured using the red and green fluorescence channels.
Use tweezers to remove a cover glass containing biofilm from the microtitre plate well.
Hold the cover glass perpendicularly over an agarose pad made of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Wash the biofilm by pipetting approximately 50 μL of PBS over the cover glass.
Allow the liquid runoff from washing to fall on the agarose pad.
Cover the agarose pad with a fresh piece of microscope cover glass.
Image using DIC and fluorescence (red and green channels) imaging modalities to analyze the washed biofilm.
Excite and emit for green fluorescence at 470 nm and capture images between 500–550 nm.
Excite and emit for red fluorescence at 510 nm and capture images between 592–668 nm.
Set fluorescent exposures to 30 ms at 30% intensity.
